title: Annotatio IV §.VIII close: Ambrose — after consecration it is Christ’s body; old creature made new — stop before §.IX
pass_a_gloss: This therefore we will establish — how that which is bread can be the body of Christ by consecration. But consecration is made by the words of the Lord, that the venerable Sacrament may be confected. You see how operative Christ’s speech is. If therefore there is such force in the Lord’s speech that (bread and wine) begin to be what they were not, and are changed into another, Therefore, that I may answer you, it was not the body of Christ before consecration, but after consecration it now is the body of Christ. He Himself spoke and it was done; YOU YOURSELF WERE, BUT YOU WERE AN OLD CREATURE; AFTER YOU HAVE BEEN CONSECRATED, YOU HAVE BEGUN TO BE A NEW CREATURE.
pass_b_english: How can what is bread be Christ’s body by consecration? By the Lord’s words the sacrament is made — Christ’s speech is operative.

If bread and wine begin to be what they were not and are changed into another, then it was not Christ’s body before consecration, but after it is. He spoke and it was done: you were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one.
Stop before §.IX (fifth century: Chrysostom and Augustine).
source_text: Hoc igitur adstruemus, quomodo qui panis est, potest esse corpus Christi consecratione. Consecratio autem fit verbis Domini, ut venerabile Sacramentum conficiatur. Vides quàm operatorius sit sermo Christi. Si ergo tanta vis est in sermone Domini, ut inciperent esse, (panis & vinum) quæ non erant, & in aliud commutentur, Ergo, ut Tibi respondeam, non erat corpus Christi ante consecrationem, sed post consecrationem jam est corpus Christi. Ipse dixit & factum est; TU IPSE ERAS, SED ERAS VETUS CREATURA; POSTQUAM CONSECRATUS ES, NOVA CREATURA ESSE CŒPISTI.
